claim: Replacing the constant start with a fine symmetric unimodal profile (N=64 log-parametrized heights, L-BFGS-B) raises R from 0.6667 to 0.7552; the optimum is a smooth central bump with positive nonuniform wings (max/mean height 1.62) and a flatter f*f top (1% share 9.3%).

Simulated annealing over N=32 heights with multiplicative/block/swap moves, seeded from an upsampled tent, reaches R=0.8404, far above symmetric local search; the resulting profile is asymmetric (max/mean 2.59, f*f peak at 0.562) and much flatter near the top (1% share 30.8%).

Random hill-climbing on N=400 heights seeded with a Gaussian bump reaches R=0.8648, the best of generation 1; the profile is strongly asymmetric (max/mean 3.53, f*f peak at 0.170) with a very flat f*f top (1% share 41.3%).

Coordinate-wise local search on upsampled heights (N=7680) reaches R=0.7938, beating short symmetric families but below the asymmetric SA/hill-climb results; its f*f peak sits at 0.581 with 1% share 21.1%.

Multiscale multiplicative hill-climbing with adaptive resolution (N=33925) reaches R=0.8106; the profile is nearly symmetric in mass (max/mean 1.80) but the f*f peak is off-center at 0.252, showing asymmetry helps even at high resolution.

All generation-1 winners are asymmetric with an off-center f*f peak (0.17-0.58), and higher R correlates with flatter f*f tops (1% share 9%->41%). Worth testing whether explicitly optimizing for a flat, off-center f*f plateau (rather than generic hill-climbing) pushes R above 0.865, and whether the true optimum is a one-sided ramp.

Replacing the Gaussian-bump seed with a discretized x^{-p} power-singularity seed (left/right/symmetric, n up to 800, p up to 0.8) inside the same hill-climb raised R from 0.8648 to 0.8743 (+0.0095); the winning profile is strongly asymmetric (max/mean 6.32) with a much flatter f*f top (1% share 42.5% vs 41.3%) and its f*f peak at 0.482. The gain is real but far short of the ~0.90 the pure x^{-1/2

Fitting a 6-parameter family (x^{-1/2} base times a quartic log-modulation plus a floor t, Nelder-Mead then L-BFGS-B, N=2000) reaches R=0.8808, the best of generation 2 (+0.0159 over its 0.8648 start). The optimum is extremely edge-concentrated (max/mean 32.2) with an off-center f*f peak at 0.086 and a very flat top (44.7% of knots within 0.1% of max). This shows a low-dimensional parametric famil

Upsampling the N=400 winner to N=2000 and adding edge-sharpening, log-block multiplicative, and re-interpolation moves barely moved R (0.8648 -> 0.8658, +0.0010). Resolution and edge moves are not the binding constraint: the shape family, not the search resolution, limits R, since the result stays near the smooth-bump basin (max/mean 3.51, f*f peak 0.424).

Gradient-based refinement of the smooth-bump basin does not escape it: analytic-gradient ascent plus hill-climbing (p0008, N=400) gave only 0.8683 (+0.0035) and L-BFGS-B in log-height space with multi-scale growth to N=4000 (p0013) gave only 0.8654 (+0.0005). Both stay in the symmetric-ish bump family (max/mean ~3.5-3.8, f*f peak 0.30-0.37), confirming that polishing a bump cannot reach the singul

Multi-resolution local search with upsampling and smooth multiplicative moves, run wide from the N=32 SA winner, produced no gain (0.84045 -> 0.84047, +0.00002). At N=32 the SA basin is already locally saturated for this move set; the wide-loop mutation did not change the shape family or resolution enough to matter.

The x^{-1/2} algebra predicts R near 0.90 for a discretized singular edge, but the best generation-2 result is 0.8808 (p0012) and the raw singular seed only 0.8743 (p0010). The gap is unexplained: worth testing whether it comes from the finite end height / floor t, the quartic modulation being too stiff, or the discrete step-function quadrature, e.g. by fitting a free monotone tail shape or a high

Freeing the exponent and raising the log-modulation to degree 8 (11 params, multi-start Nelder-Mead+L-BFGS-B at N=1200, scored to N=8000) gave zero gain over p0012 (0.880755 -> 0.880755). Family stiffness is not the binding constraint on the ~0.88 plateau; the richer family just re-converges to the same shape.

Direct log-space L-BFGS-B over all N heights with an exact analytic gradient, started inside p0012's singular-edge basin (N=2000 then 4000), gained only +0.0008 (0.880755 -> 0.881554). The parametric ansatz is not the limiter: the singular-edge basin is locally saturated for free-form gradient ascent, so the ~0.02 gap to the ~0.90 algebra bound is not a stiffness or parametrization artifact.

Adding a second power singularity at the right end (a*u^-p + b*(1-u)^-q + c, multi-start Nelder-Mead/L-BFGS-B at N=2000, rebuilt to N=8000) gained only +0.0008 (0.880755 -> 0.881554). Two-edge structure does not beat the single x^{-1/2} edge, so the single-edge ansatz is not structurally wrong.

Multi-resolution projected gradient ascent with an analytic gradient of R, plus adaptive step/restart, from p0012 at N=1000 gave only +0.0001 (0.880755 -> 0.880875). Gradient ascent on the singular-edge basin is saturated regardless of step control.

Direct analytic-gradient ascent on step heights with progressive upsampling (800->12800), smoothing and perturbed restarts, from p0012, produced no gain (0.880755 -> 0.880755). Upsampling and perturbation do not escape the singular-edge basin, consistent with resolution not being the constraint.

All four generation-3 attacks on the ~0.88 plateau (richer family, free-form gradient, two-edge, multi-resolution ascent) land within +0.0008 of p0012, so the ~0.02 gap to the ~0.90 algebra bound is not stiffness, parametrization, or single-edge structure. Worth testing whether it is finite-N quadrature (the f*f peak sits at 0.057-0.086 of support, near the edge where discretization is coarsest) o

Replacing p0019's two-edge family with a vanishing right edge u^{-p}(1-u)^q exp(quartic) (9 params, multi-start NM+L-BFGS-B at N=2000, then free-form log-space polish to N=4000) gained only +0.00009 (0.881554 -> 0.881645). The vanishing-edge tail structure does not break the ~0.8816 plateau; the jump edge is effectively optimal for this objective.

A perturbed-restart loop (block/full log-normal noise sigma 0.1-0.3, L-BFGS-B, periodic N=8000 polish, run to 0.9*budget) from p0015 found no escape: best 0.881619 (+0.00007). The 0.8816 level is a local max of the free-form problem under this perturbation scale, not a budget-limited artifact.

Resolving the singular edge at N=10000 then 20000 with FFT-accelerated convolution and log-space L-BFGS-B gave only +0.00007 (0.881554 -> 0.881620), and the run used just 2.0 s of 30 s. Finite-N quadrature is not the binding constraint; the continuum optimum near the singular-edge basin is ~0.8816.

Progressive multistage resolution refinement (2000->20000) with exact L-BFGS-B gradient, continuing until the deadline rather than stopping early, gave the best generation-4 result: 0.881681 (+0.00013 over p0015). The gain is marginal but real, and the f*f peak landed at 0.448 (vs 0.057 for p0015), confirming the plateau is reachable from multiple f*f-peak positions.

Gradient ascent with momentum, extra upsample stages, and larger perturbation kicks from p0012 reached only 0.880922 (+0.00017). Momentum and kicks do not escape the singular-edge basin; the ~0.88 level is robust to this class of moves.

Five independent generation-4 attacks on the ~0.8816 level (vanishing right edge, perturbed restarts, N=20000 resolution, deadline-driven multistage, momentum+kicks) all land within +0.00013, and the best (p0020, 0.881681) still leaves ~0.018 to the ~0.90 algebra bound. The plateau is a genuine local max of the free-form problem, so the remaining gap likely needs a structurally different shape cla

Tighter L-BFGS-B tolerances (ftol 1e-16, gtol 1e-12, maxcor 30) plus repeated L-BFGS restarts until no improvement, at fixed N=20000 with fftconvolve, gave the best generation-5 result: 0.881937 (+0.000317 over p0023's 0.881620). The f*f top is ~49% of knots within 1% of max with the peak at 0.366 of support. This is the largest single gain on the ~0.8816 plateau found so far, showing the plateau

Enforcing per-stage deadlines with fftconvolve up to N=32000 (stages 1000..32000, best-iterate kept on timeout) gained only +0.000079 (0.881681 -> 0.881761) and used just 4.5 s of 30 s. Merely reaching higher N with a staged schedule does not move the plateau; the gain in p0026 came from tolerance/restart polish, not resolution.

Pushing to N=64000 with fftconvolve, larger progressive stages (4000..64000) and a final L-BFGS restart polish gained only +0.000022 (0.881681 -> 0.881704). Very high resolution (N=64000) is not the binding constraint; the ~0.8816-0.8819 level is shape-limited, not resolution-limited.

A 3-singular-edge family (sum of three w_j (u-s_j)^{-1/2} terms with free interior positions s_2,s_3, times a quartic exp modulation, 10 params, multi-start NM+L-BFGS-B at N=2000 then polish at N=4000) gained only +0.000023 (0.881554 -> 0.881577). Superposing multiple singular edges does not extend the flat f*f region enough to beat a single edge; the multi-singularity hypothesis is refuted.

p-norm soft-max annealing (p=4..128) at N=2000 to smooth the hard max before hard-max refinement was killed by signal 24 (CPU limit 47 s / memory 1500 MB) before producing a score. The soft-max escape route remains untested: the run failed on resource limits, not on the objective, so a leaner implementation is needed to test whether non-smooth max traps the optimizer.

Generation 5 splits the plateau attacks cleanly: resolution-only pushes (N=32000, N=64000) gain <=+0.00008, multi-singularity families gain +0.00002, but tolerance/restart polish at fixed N=20000 gains +0.00032 (p0026, 0.881937). Worth testing whether combining p0026's tight-tolerance restart loop with p0030's high-N stages (polish at N=32000-64000 with ftol 1e-16 and repeated restarts) pushes pas

Direct log-space L-BFGS-B with exact analytic gradient, run as a perturb-escape loop at N=8000 from p0019's two-edge start, reaches 0.881986 (+0.000433 over its 0.881554 start) — the best generation-6 result and the first attack to beat p0026's 0.881937. The winning f*f has 49.42% of knots within 1% of max with the peak at 0.265, so the gain comes from reshaping the shoulders of a flat-topped prof

A p=4->3->2 homotopy on the concentration functional Phi_p = int(L^p)/(M^{p-1} int L) with exact analytic gradient at N=20000, followed by exact-R polish, gains +0.000024 over p0026 (0.881937 -> 0.881961). The gain is small but positive, showing the sharper p>2 surrogate does shift the optimum slightly toward steeper shoulders; it does not close the gap to the ~0.90 algebra bound.

An N=20000 -> N=40000 -> N=20000 round trip with maxcor=100 inside p0026's tight-tolerance restart loop gained only +0.000010 (0.881937 -> 0.881947) and used 11.4 s of 30 s. The N=20000 optimum is already fully resolved; extra resolution round-trips are not the binding constraint.

Re-polishing the 3-singular-edge basin (p0029's 4000-step heights) at N=20000 with p0026's tight-tolerance polisher plus an N=40000 round trip was killed by signal 24 (CPU/memory limit) before scoring. The multi-edge basin remains untested at high resolution with the best polisher; the failure is resource, not evidence against the basin.

Skipping upsampling when the start is already fine-grained and spending nearly all budget on repeated L-BFGS restarts at fixed N=64000 with growing memory (maxcor=40) gains +0.000211 (0.881704 -> 0.881915). Restart polish at high fixed N is a reliable small-gain move, consistent with p0026's tolerance/restart result.

Generation 6 splits cleanly: direct log-gradient perturb-escape at N=8000 (p0033, +0.000433) and fixed-N restart polish (p0032, +0.000211) beat tolerance/restart at N=20000 (p0026, +0.000317) and homotopy (p0035, +0.000024), while resolution round-trips (p0036, +0.000010) do nothing. Worth testing whether a perturb-escape loop at N=8000 seeded from p0033's winner, combined with p0035's p-homotopy

Adding the p=4->3->2 Phi_p homotopy (analytic gradient, adopted only when exact R improves) inside p0033's N=8000 perturb-escape loop gave zero gain (0.881986 -> 0.881986, start unchanged). Reshaping the flat-top objective does not help once the singular-edge basin is already found; the hard-max R gradient is not the binding constraint at this level.

Escalating resolution inside p0033's escape loop (three timed stages N=8000/20000/40000 sharing one global best-by-exact-R) gained only +0.000001 (0.881986 -> 0.881987) and shifted the f*f peak from 0.265 to 0.404 without improving R. N=8000 was not the binding constraint on the escape loop; the basin is resolution-saturated.

Replacing p0033's iid sigma=0.02 jitter with structured block-multiplicative kicks (3-8 blocks, sigma 0.05-0.30, plus every-5th half-support sigma=0.5 kick) produced no escape: 0.881986 -> 0.881986, same f*f peak at 0.265. Coarse block kicks do not move the singular-edge basin either; the ~0.882 level resists both local and block perturbations.

All three generation-7 attacks on p0033's basin (Phi_p homotopy, resolution escalation to N=40000, structured block kicks) land within +0.000001 of 0.881986, so the escape move, the objective shape, and resolution are all non-binding there. Periodic upsampling to N=128000 inside p0032's fixed-N restart polish gained only +0.000018 (0.881915 -> 0.881933), and alternating N=20000/40000 polishes with larger memory on stalls gained +0.000026 (0.881947 -> 0.881973). Both confirm the ~0.882 level is saturated against resolution and restart-schedule tweaks at fixed shape.
